subject: Model fit evals & Redwood-verified benchmarks
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit evals & benchmark links — Redwood follow-up

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion on your summarization and retrieval-heavy use cases. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Ask / goals: reduce hallucination for long-context summaries, keep p99 latency under 800ms for interactive flows, and support ~200 TPS during peak batch scoring.
- Recommended starting models for evaluation: Redwood-6B-quant (4-bit), Redwood-13B-pt (fp16), and a smaller Redwood-2.7B for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- I've attached the prompt set you mentioned (acme_prompt_set_v1.txt); we'll also run these through our standard eval harness.

What I attached / links:
- acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (attached) — the prompt variations you shared + a few edge-case prompts we suggested.
- I'm running the initial benchmark now and will upload a Redwood-verified profile report by EOD Tuesday. In the meantime, here's the dashboard link for our standard model profiles: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-analytics-20260804

Proposed next actions: 
1) I'll run the prompt set across the three recommended model variants and share a short report (p50/p90/p99 latencies, token throughput, quality metrics) by Tue 8/4.
2) Schedule a 45-min debrief Wed 8/5 — tentatively 10:00am PT — to go over results and tradeoffs. Please confirm if that works.
3) If the results look good, we can spin up a short dedicated benchmark window on Dedicated capacity to simulate production TPS.

If you want additional metrics (e.g., headroom, warm/cold start impact), call that out and I’ll add them.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

---

Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700

Thanks Alex — appreciate the quick recap. A couple quick clarifications before your run: 

- Can you include TPS (tokens/sec and requests/sec) numbers both for steady-state and peak burst (1-min avg)? We need to validate our latency SLOs at ~200 TPS.
- Please include latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99) for both cold-start and warmed KV-cache scenarios.
- We've seen quality regressions on a small set of prompts when switching from Model A -> Model B in another vendor's stack. Can you add a short 'regression check' on the prompt set (flag samples where answer diverges materially from baseline) and include a handful of examples in the report?

Wed 8/5 10:00am PT works for us for the debrief.

One more ask — can you share the Redwood-verified performance profile (TPS, latency percentiles) for the 13B variant you mentioned, and any quantized variant performance notes? That will help our infra team plan capacity.

Thanks,
Sam Jenkins
Senior Product Manager
Acme Analytics
sam.jenkins@acme-analytics.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & benchmark links — Redwood follow-up

Hi Sam / Priya —

Quick update: I finished the first pass of the runs against the acme_prompt_set_v1.txt you provided. Core highlights (summary) — full PDF attached (redwood_bench_report_20260804.pdf) and live profile: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-analytics-20260804

Summary (short):
- Redwood-6B-quant (4-bit, optimized kernels): steady-state ~480 reqs/sec (approx. 950 tokens/sec depending on prompt length), burst 1-min avg ~620 reqs/sec. Latency (warmed KV-cache): p50 42ms, p90 128ms, p99 330ms. Cold-start p99 spikes to ~780ms for long-context runs.
- Redwood-13B-pt (fp16): steady-state ~120 reqs/sec (~2300 tokens/sec), burst ~150 reqs/sec. Latency (warmed): p50 88ms, p90 210ms, p99 560ms. Cold-start p99 ~920ms.
- Redwood-2.7B (low-latency): steady-state ~900 reqs/sec, p50 18ms, p90 60ms, p99 160ms (good option for low-latency front-end use-cases; quality tradeoffs noted in PDF).

Quality/regression checks:
- We ran a divergence/regression check against your baseline outputs (attached as sample_diffs.txt in the PDF appendix). ~4% of prompts showed materially different summaries between 13B and 6B-quant; in most cases 13B improved factuality, but there were 3 examples where the 13B introduced a concise but incorrect entity — flagged in the report with suggested prompt modifications.

What this means for your SLOs: based on the numbers above, the 6B-quant meets your 200 TPS target comfortably in steady-state and has some headroom for bursts if you reserve Dedicated capacity or leverage autoscaling with warm caches. If strict p99 < 800ms is required under cold-start heavy workloads, we recommend a small warm pool (keep-alive) or the 2.7B for interactive endpoints.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) 30-min technical debrief Wed 8/5 10:00am PT (confirmed on our side).
2) If you want, Marissa (cc'd) can scope a short Dedicated benchmark window to hit your 1-min burst targets and produce pricing.
3) We can run a follow-up regression sweep focused on the 3 flagged prompts after applying prompt edits; that typically clears up most hallucination regressions.

Attaching: redwood_bench_report_20260804.pdf (contains full metrics, sample diffs, and methodology).

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.ai
